turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Meredith stops just inside the door and doesn't sit.

"Mr. Hale? Meredith Kalinowski. You asked for this meeting. I have until 4:40.

My son found out he had a zero from the gradebook, on his phone, in the middle of class. Nobody called me first.

So I'll start with the basics. Who decided on the zero, when, and on what basis?"
I spoke with the vice principal before you came in.

"Before I came in." She lets that sit. "So the vice principal was consulted before I was. Before Owen was.

Which vice principal? When did you speak with them? Was it before or after the zero went into the gradebook?

And is there anything in writing? I'll want that in an email."
She's backing me completely. Policy is policy, and it isn't up to you.

"'Policy is policy.'" Her voice doesn't change. "Then it'll be easy to show me. Which policy? Section number, and the date it was last revised.

You've told me what she thinks. I haven't heard what the policy says about a student being heard before a zero goes in. Was Owen heard first? Did anyone sit down with him before it posted?

And 'it isn't up to you.' Okay. Whose is it, then?"

She takes a pen out of her bag but doesn't open anything.
So frankly, this meeting is a courtesy.

"'A courtesy.'" She finally opens a notebook and writes the word down. "Noted.

So the decision was made, the zero was posted, and I'm here as a courtesy. That's the sequence, and I'll want it confirmed in writing.

If I'm not here to be heard, why did you ask for this meeting? What do you want from me, Mr. Hale?

And since it's a courtesy: what do you have on my son's essay? Not the checker's number. What did you see?"
